package_info.why_malicious: Malicious JavaScript is injected into Magento e-commerce checkout pages to capture and exfiltrate customers' payment information to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling large-scale credit card theft (Magecart-style attack).

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within Magento e-commerce CMS checkout page templates

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious JavaScript injected into e-commerce checkout pages to steal payment information (exact code not provided in report).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user loads the checkout page, the injected JavaScript accesses payment form fields in the DOM, collects sensitive payment data (such as credit card numbers), and sends this data via HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to an attacker-controlled external domain, resulting in exfiltration of customer payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The JavaScript code is designed to capture sensitive payment data directly from user input fields and transmit it to an external, untrusted server. This behavior is a hallmark of Magecart and other web skimming attacks, which specifically target e-commerce platforms to steal credit card information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should only transmit payment data to trusted, PCI-compliant payment processors or gateways, never to unknown or untrusted external domains. Code in checkout pages should not access or exfiltrate raw payment details outside of secure payment flows.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) may collect payment data via JavaScript, but only to securely transmit it to their own PCI-compliant endpoints. Such scripts are well-documented, loaded from trusted sources, and do not obfuscate their network destinations.
key_indicators: JavaScript code accessing or reading payment form fields (e.g., credit card number, CVV, expiration date)
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from checkout pages to domains not associated with the merchant or known payment processors
Injected or obfuscated JavaScript code present in Magento CMS template files
Unexpected <script> tags or inline event handlers in checkout page source code

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into Magento e-commerce website checkout page templates.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and executed in customers' browsers during the checkout process.

attack_chain.action: The injected JavaScript captures payment information entered by users into the checkout form fields.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive payment data (e.g., credit card details) is collected in the browser.

attack_chain.action: The captured payment data is exfiltrated via HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credit card data and can monetize it through fraud or resale.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code accessing or reading payment form fields on checkout pages
Unexpected or unauthorized network requests from checkout pages to external domains not associated with payment processing
Presence of obfuscated or injected JavaScript in Magento CMS template files
file_indicators: Injected or obfuscated JavaScript code within Magento CMS template files (e.g., app/design/frontend/*/template/checkout/*.phtml)
Unexpected <script> tags or inline event handlers in checkout page HTML source
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from checkout pages to domains or IPs not associated with the merchant or known payment processors
Connections to domains or IPs previously linked to Magecart or web skimming infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor e-commerce checkout pages for unauthorized or obfuscated JavaScript, especially code that accesses payment form fields and initiates network requests to untrusted domains. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) and strict Content Security Policies (CSPs) to block unauthorized script injections and prevent outbound data exfiltration. Regularly audit Magento CMS template files for unexpected code changes or additions.
